writeup.headline: Modine rates Sell: strong data center growth, but weak trend, thin underlying cash flow and debt weigh.
writeup.thesis: Modine scores 42, a Sell, 3 points below the Hold band. Growth is the strongest factor (65), with TTM revenue growth of 29.5% and latest-quarter revenue growth of 28.0% year on year, though growth slowed by 19.4 pp from the previous quarter. Quality (44) and the balance sheet (30) hold the score back. Excluding customer prepayments, the FCF margin is -1.6% against a reported 3.0%, net debt is 4.34 times FCF, and cash covers only 0.18 of debt. On valuation (36), absolute levels are not low: P/S of 2.1, EV/EBIT of 22.5, and an FCF yield 5.7 pp below the 10-year Treasury yield. Against its own history, valuation sits near the middle of its own history (P/FCF not comparable). The trend score of 15 is the weakest factor, with the price 55.5% below its 52-week high and 36.8% below its 200-day average.
key_risks: Cash flow leans on customer prepayments: contract liabilities rose $163.5M, and underlying FCF is negative.
Leverage is meaningful, with net debt at 4.34 times FCF and cash covering 0.18 of debt.
Customer concentration around the $4B+ data center capacity agreement, flagged by Cantor.
Higher copper, steel and freight costs and tight component supply could pressure a 22.2% gross margin.
The share price is falling sharply, 51.5 pp behind SPY over the last 126 trading days.
what_would_change: A 3-point gain would lift the rating to Hold, for example from a stabilizing share price trend or positive FCF excluding prepayments.
Q2 results on Nov 3 and new multi-year targets at the Nov 18 investor day could shift the growth and news scores.
Further slowing of revenue growth, or weaker margins and balance sheet scores, would push the score toward the Strong Sell line, 13 points lower.
